setupSteps: Choose the surface. For the beginner version, use a kitchen counter or a heavy, fixed bench, about hip height (the surface should be at or just below your hip crease when standing; higher is easier; est.). Press down on it hard to check it does not slide, tip or wobble. Avoid a rolling chair, a stool on tiles, or a table with loose legs.

Floor and noise: a non-slip floor for the feet. In a flat with neighbours below, put a yoga mat or thick rug where the feet will land and keep the knee drives slow. Avoid early morning and late night with the fast floor version.
Footwear: flat trainers, or bare feet on a non-slip mat. Avoid socks on smooth tiles (the foot can slide out).

Hand position: place your hands on the edge of the surface about shoulder-width apart (Strengthlog), directly under the shoulders (Healthline: shoulders directly over the wrists), fingers spread, pointing forward.

Walk the feet back: step both feet back until your arms are straight, your body forms a slanted straight line from head through hips to heels, and your shoulders are above or just ahead of your wrists. Feet about hip-width apart (est.).
Brace: gently pull the belly button towards the spine, squeeze the buttocks lightly, and press the floor of your palms into the surface so the shoulder blades spread slightly.
Head and eyes: neck in line with the spine; look at a spot just beyond your hands (Healthline suggests a spot just in front of the hands on the floor).
Clothing: a fitted top and track pants or leggings so the camera can see the hips and knees; avoid loose kurtas that hang down and hide the body line.
Water and fan: keep water within reach; the heart rate climbs quickly in the faster versions.

steps.part: A. Slow, quiet, hands-elevated mountain climber (beginner main version)
steps.title: Take the incline plank
steps.action: Hands on the counter or bench, arms straight, feet back, body in one slanted line.
steps.feel: Light firmness in the belly and the front of the shoulders; the arms do not burn.
steps.visualCheck: Side: ear, shoulder, hip and ankle form one straight line. Front: shoulders level, hands shoulder-width.

steps.part: A. Slow, quiet, hands-elevated mountain climber (beginner main version)
steps.title: Brace and shift weight
steps.action: Gently tighten your stomach and press into both hands; let the weight rest over the left foot and both hands.
steps.visualCheck: Side: hips do not rise or sink; front: hips level.

steps.part: A. Slow, quiet, hands-elevated mountain climber (beginner main version)
steps.title: Lift the right foot slightly
steps.action: Lift the right foot an inch or two off the floor, keeping the leg low.
steps.feel: A little work in the left thigh and the belly.
steps.visualCheck: Side: the body line does not change.

steps.part: A. Slow, quiet, hands-elevated mountain climber (beginner main version)
steps.title: Draw the right knee in slowly
steps.action: Slide the right knee forward and slightly up towards your right elbow or chest, as far as you can without the hips rising or the back rounding. Do not hop.
steps.feel: Lower belly and front of the hip working; the knee moves in a smooth arc.
steps.breathing: Continue breathing out as the knee comes in.
steps.visualCheck: Side: the knee goes under or in front of the hip; shoulders stay above the hands; hips stay in line.

steps.part: A. Slow, quiet, hands-elevated mountain climber (beginner main version)
steps.title: Touch the toe down softly, then return the foot
steps.action: Press the right foot back along the floor, or lift it back, until the leg is nearly straight and the toes touch softly.
steps.feel: Back of the thigh and buttock working; no stamp.
steps.breathing: Breathe in as the leg goes back.
steps.visualCheck: Side: the leg ends nearly straight and the body line returns to a slanted straight line.

steps.part: A. Slow, quiet, hands-elevated mountain climber (beginner main version)
steps.title: Repeat on the left
steps.action: Lift the left foot, draw the knee in, return.
steps.feel: A steady, easy rhythm with the trunk still.
steps.breathing: Out as the knee comes in, in as it goes back (est.; any steady pattern is fine, never hold your breath).
steps.visualCheck: Front: hips level, no side-to-side sway; side: hips do not bob.

steps.part: A. Slow, quiet, hands-elevated mountain climber (beginner main version)
steps.title: Finish the set
steps.action: Step both feet in, stand up and walk around.
steps.feel: Heart rate up, breathing quicker, but you can still speak in short sentences.
steps.visualCheck: Stand tall; shake out the wrists.

steps.title: Start in a high plank, hands under the shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels (Healthline)
Drive one knee in towards the chest, keeping the hips down and level
Return that foot and switch legs in a smooth running rhythm; pick the pace so the hips do not rise (Livestrong, Hinge Health)
Keep the shoulders over the wrists and the neck neutral; stop the set when the hips start to rise or sag

commonMistakes.title: Hips rising (pike)
commonMistakes.text: Hips rising (pike). Why: it takes tension off the core and shifts work to the shoulders (FitnessVolt advice; sources say hips often rise as you tire or speed up). Fix: slow down; keep the body in one line; stop the set when you cannot.

commonMistakes.title: Hips sagging
commonMistakes.text: Hips sagging. Why: the lower back arches and takes the load (a physical therapist quoted by Livestrong). Fix: squeeze the buttocks lightly and brace the belly; raise the hands higher to make it easier.

commonMistakes.title: Rushing so the form breaks down
commonMistakes.text: Rushing so the form breaks down. Why: speed usually causes poor form, especially the hips shifting above the rest of the body (a trainer quoted in a news piece), and bouncing on the toes adds impact (Hinge Health). Fix: begin at one drive every 1-2 seconds and add speed only when the line stays straight.

commonMistakes.title: Bouncing shoulders or hands too far forward or too wide
commonMistakes.text: Bouncing shoulders or hands too far forward or too wide. Why: strains the wrists and shoulders and stops the core doing the work. Fix: hands shoulder-width, directly beneath the shoulders; press the surface away.

commonMistakes.title: Short knee drive or crossing the feet
commonMistakes.text: Short knee drive or crossing the feet. Why: reduced range and balance loss (Livestrong and others). Fix: drive the knee forward and under you; keep feet hip-width.

commonMistakes.title: Stamping or hopping the feet
commonMistakes.text: Stamping or hopping the feet. Why: noise and joint shock, especially in a flat with neighbours below. Fix: lift the foot slightly and slide it back; use a mat.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Why: breath-holding raises blood pressure more than breathing during effort. Fix: breathe out as the knee comes in; talk-test.

commonMistakes.title: Using a wobbly surface for the beginner version
commonMistakes.text: Using a wobbly surface for the beginner version. Why: a sliding or tipping surface can cause a fall onto the face or wrists. Fix: choose a fixed counter or heavy bench and test it first.

safetyNotes: Wrist, elbow or shoulder problems: use a higher surface, forearms on the surface, or the standing knee drive; avoid bearing weight if it hurts.
Back problems: keep the stomach braced and ribs down; use the incline version; stop if the lower back arches or hurts. Hinge Health advises checking with a provider if back pain is significant.
High blood pressure and heart disease: light-to-moderate effort, steady breathing, avoid breath-holding; get clearance if BP is severe or uncontrolled or you have known heart disease.
Pregnancy and postpartum: the plank position loads the front belly wall; ask your obstetrician or women's health physiotherapist first, and stop if the belly bulges or domes.
Recent surgery, dizziness, balance problems: only with approval.
Osteoporosis: wrists and spine are in a weight-bearing position; use the incline version and avoid spinal bending; get individual advice.
